tax.text: Alvarez voted for ACA 1, which proposed easing voter-approval thresholds for specified local taxes and bonds funding affordable housing and public infrastructure.
tax.quote: Addis, Aguiar-Curry, Alvarez, Arambula, Bauer-Kahan, Bennett, Berman, Boerner, Bonta, Bryan, Calderon, Juan Carrillo

wages.text: Alvarez voted for SB 525, which established phased minimum-wage increases for health-care workers.
wages.quote: Addis, Aguiar-Curry, Alvarez, Arambula, Bains, Bauer-Kahan, Bennett, Berman

housing.text: Alvarez authored bills to accelerate housing construction by shortening reviews and limiting procedural delays.
housing.quote: These bills cut through bureaucratic delay and legal loopholes to ensure we build housing faster, smarter, and more fairly.

schools.text: Alvarez voted for a state budget that increased TK-12 funding and expanded district before- and after-school programs.
schools.quote: David voted for a State Budget that includes a historic investment in TK-12th grade education.

safety.text: Alvarez sought funding for both nonprofit prevention and outreach services and the Police Department's Homeless Outreach Team.
safety.quote: supplementary general funds are needed to ensure that year round outreach services are provided by both outside organizations and the Police Department’s Homeless Outreach Team

sentencing.text: Alvarez requested expansion of a program providing treatment, housing, and community services to low-level misdemeanor offenders instead of custody.
sentencing.quote: SMART provides access to drug treatment services while providing housing, the elements necessary for a successful recovery. The program prioritizes the provision of services and works to ensure that the homeless are not criminalized.

immigration.text: Alvarez authored AB 2586 to permit undocumented students at California public colleges and universities to obtain campus employment.
immigration.quote: Students who are legally allowed to study at California’s public colleges and universities should also be allowed to work to pay for their own education.

guns.text: Alvarez voted for SB 2, which tightened concealed-carry licensing requirements and restricted carrying firearms in specified locations.
guns.quote: Addis, Aguiar-Curry, Alvarez, Arambula, Bauer-Kahan, Bennett, Berman, Boerner

abortion.text: Alvarez voted for SCA 10, which placed constitutional protections for abortion and contraception before California voters.
abortion.quote: Aguiar-Curry, Alvarez, Arambula, Bauer-Kahan, Bennett, Berman, Bloom, Boerner Horvath

gender.text: Alvarez voted for AB 1955, which bars schools from requiring disclosure of a student's gender identity or expression without the student's consent.
gender.quote: Addis, Aguiar-Curry, Alvarez, Arambula, Bains, Bauer-Kahan, Bennett, Berman

cannabis.text: Alvarez voted for AB 1775, which expanded regulated cannabis consumption lounges by allowing locally approved food sales and live performances.
cannabis.quote: Addis, Aguiar-Curry, Alanis, Alvarez, Arambula, Bauer-Kahan, Bennett, Berman

health.text: Alvarez voted for SB 770, directing state work toward a unified health-care financing system that could include single-payer financing.
health.quote: Addis, Aguiar-Curry, Alvarez, Arambula, Bauer-Kahan, Bennett, Berman, Boerner

energy.text: Alvarez sought funding and staffing to implement a climate plan targeting 100% renewable energy.
energy.quote: San Diego demonstrated leadership when it adopted the Climate Action Plan with the ambitious goal of 100% renewable energy.

voting.text: Alvarez voted for SB 1174, which prohibited local governments from requiring identification when voters cast or submit ballots.
voting.quote: Addis, Aguiar-Curry, Alvarez, Arambula, Bains, Bauer-Kahan, Bennett, Berman

wages.text: He objected to union-only bidding rules that barred his nonunion business from school projects.
wages.quote: One example that really bothered me is because I am not a union shop, I cannot bid on any school projects because they are union-only, which in my opinion is a favor by local politicians to their number one contributors

housing.text: He made expanding affordable housing, including using surplus government property, one of his top three priorities.
housing.quote: Galicia said his top three priorities would be finding solutions to the Tijuana River Valley crisis and endorsing it as a Superfund site; updating and improving the county's emergency response plan; and enhanced short- and long-term approaches to homelessness, including more affordable homes and utilizing surplus government property.

safety.text: Galicia criticized criminalizing and relocating unhoused people as ineffective rather than addressing the underlying problem.
safety.quote: As businesses, we are surrounded by those people, and they are dealing with it is that they are criminalizing it. You kick them out of a certain area. How do you make that illegal. It does not solve the issue. It makes people feel better.

immigration.text: He criticized federal policy that allows migrants to enter and then releases them into cities without support or a coherent plan.
immigration.quote: That is an issue that the federal government should have a much better grasp on. This thing where they let them all come in, and then street releases them at a random intersection in a city and lets them go, is abandoning people and their fate.
